Build Dexterous Hands

Turning innovation into real-world application



What is RoboHANDS?

Robotic hands are central to general-purpose robotics, enabling dexterous interaction with the physical world. They are increasingly important in humanoid robots and assistive applications, including intelligent prosthetic hands. Advances in mechanics, materials, sensing, control, and AI are enabling more capable and adaptive manipulation, bringing robotic hands closer to reliable real-world deployment.

RoboHANDS offers a unique platform for researchers and engineers to exchange ideas on emerging technologies, address key technical challenges, and advance robotic hand capabilities. We invite contributions on the following topics:

Design, Mechanisms & Actuation

Hand architectures, mechanical design, kinematic structures, actuation and transmission, and manufacturing, including bio-inspired design, multifingered hands, adaptive grippers, soft actuation, and morphological intelligence.

Sensing & Physical Intelligence

Tactile and multimodal sensing, sensor integration, contact and slip detection, and physical intelligence for interaction with objects and environments.

Dexterous Manipulation, Modeling, Control & Learning

Dexterous grasping and in-hand manipulation, contact dynamics and simulation, motion and force control under uncertainty, and learning-based methods for skill acquisition, generalization, and adaptation across tasks, objects, and embodiments.

Special Focus: Hand Exoskeletons

This special focus covers hand exoskeleton systems, including wearable design, actuation and control, human–exoskeleton interaction, and intelligent, adaptive assistance for hand rehabilitation, functional assistance, and dexterity enhancement.
